driver_scores.evidence_basis: Singapore's carbon tax was a direct policy intervention that changed economic incentives by placing a price on emissions.
The policy particularly affected emissions-intensive industrial and energy-related facilities, including refining and petrochemical activities.
Compliance obligations and emissions reporting created operational adjustments, but not the dominant transmission channel.

final_attribution.summary: SG-CARBON-TAX-2019 is classified as a policy-native replay case. The primary attribution is MKT_006 because the carbon tax was a government policy mechanism that changed incentives and costs through emissions pricing.

mechanism_summary.dominant_mechanism: Policy cost signalling through carbon pricing.
supporting_mechanisms: carbon pricing encouraged efficiency and lower-emissions behaviour
energy-related sectors were more exposed due to emissions intensity
compliance and reporting created operational adjustment requirements
